reference: GNU find on the runner's reference PATH is the independent oracle for parity cases. The runner validates each script status against GNU find, compares stdout bytes and the resulting fixture tree, including modes and links. The metadata contract uses Bash type/help builtins and the documented loadable registry; it is not counted as operation coverage.
coverage: Bounded depth and default -print on a small nested relative tree.
POSIX -depth postorder, default -print, and traversal effects across Boolean branches and starting paths.
Boolean expression grouping, basename globs, and -prune traversal control.
-P, -L, and -H behavior on an ordinary directory symlink without a cycle.
Byte-size boundaries, exact and symbolic permission masks, and -empty.
Documented -printf escapes for path, relative path, basename, dirname, type, and byte size.
NUL-delimited output for a filename containing a newline.
Safe -exec ; and -exec + argument substitution using printf only.
Postorder -delete of relative entries inside the disposable fixture tree.
GNU error status for a missing starting path and an -L symlink cycle.
Bash type/help metadata contract; xdev mount-boundary behavior is deferred.
Additional bounded regular-file, hardlink, symlink and multi-operand error continuation regressions.
Guest pass 4 G57: find -newermt shares date's parser, with TZ="ZONE" prefixes and zone-plus-offset items.
exclusions: No host or system paths, mount operations, network activity, devices, credentials, or process-control operations are used.
-xdev requires a distinct mounted filesystem and is recorded as deferred.
The suite does not qualify time predicates, ownership lookup, every file type, GNU's full -printf language, or predicates documented as out of scope (-links, -inum, and -anewer).

cases.purpose: Check bounded recursive traversal, both depth limits, and find's default -print action on a tree with files and directories at several depths.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/one/two tree/two
printf a > tree/top
printf b > tree/one/mid
printf c > tree/one/two/deep
printf d > tree/two/other
find tree -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -type f

cases.purpose: Check that -depth takes no argument, is true for default printing, and visits descendants before each directory.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
printf x > tree/sub/item
find tree -depth

cases.purpose: Check that -depth sets postorder for all roots even in a branch skipped by short-circuit evaluation, and that -prune is true without blocking descent.
cases.script:
mkdir -p first/sub second/sub
printf x > first/sub/item
printf y > second/sub/item
find first second \( -prune -print \) -o \( ! -depth \)

cases.purpose: Check explicit Boolean grouping and short-circuit -prune so a matching subtree is neither printed nor descended into.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/cache/sub tree/src tree/keep
printf cache > tree/cache/sub/ignored.txt
printf source > tree/src/kept.txt
printf keep > tree/keep/also.txt
find tree -path 'tree/cache' -prune -o \( -type f -name '*.txt' \) -print

cases.purpose: Compare physical, full-follow, and command-line-argument-follow traversal on one relative directory symlink.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/real
printf data > tree/real/item
ln -s real tree/alias
find -P tree -type l
find -L tree -maxdepth 2 -type f
find -H tree/alias -maxdepth 2 -type f

cases.purpose: Check byte-count size predicates, exact and symbolic permission matching, and empty-file/empty-directory detection.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/empty-dir
printf 1234 > tree/exact
printf 12 > tree/small
: > tree/empty-file
(umask 077; printf private > tree/private)
find tree -type f -size 4c -perm 0644
find tree -type f -size +2c -perm -u+rw
find tree -empty

cases.purpose: Check the documented subset of -printf against GNU find for full and root-relative paths, basename, dirname, type, size, and newline escaping.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
printf abc > 'tree/sub/name with space'
find tree -type f -printf '%p|%P|%f|%h|%y|%s\n'

cases.purpose: Check that -print0 safely delimits a single relative path whose filename contains an embedded newline.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
name=$'line\nbreak'
printf x > "tree/$name"
find tree -type f -print0

cases.purpose: Check literal {} substitution, preservation of spaces and shell metacharacters in a filename, and both per-entry and batched -exec using only printf.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree
name='a space * $(literal)'
printf x > "tree/$name"
find "tree/$name" -exec printf '<%s>\n' 'pre{}post' \;
find "tree/$name" -exec printf '[%s]\n' '{}' +

cases.purpose: Check that -delete removes matched files and then their now-empty descendants in postorder while -mindepth preserves the fixture root; all effects stay inside the disposable relative tree.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/a/b tree/c
printf x > tree/a/b/file
printf y > tree/c/file
find tree -mindepth 1 -delete

cases.purpose: Check GNU find's nonzero status and diagnostic when a relative command-line starting path does not exist.
cases.script: find absent

cases.purpose: Check GNU find -L cycle reporting and nonzero status on a minimal relative symlink loop, without following the loop indefinitely.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
printf x > tree/sub/file
ln -s .. tree/sub/back
find -L tree -type f

cases.purpose: Check Bash's documented type/help metadata for the registered find loadable without invoking a search operation.
cases.script:
builtin type -t find
if builtin help -s find >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  builtin printf 'help=available\n'
else
  builtin printf 'help=missing\n'
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Exercise -xdev/-mount on a directory tree containing a second filesystem.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM that can create or mount a second filesystem beneath a relative fixture path, then run GNU find and the candidate against it. The provided runner forbids mount operations and offers only a single-filesystem fixture; no mount was attempted here.

cases.purpose: Missing starting paths must report failure while valid paths before and after are searched.
cases.script:
printf first > first
printf last > last
find first absent last

cases.purpose: Dangling symlinks remain searchable under -P, -H, and -L.
cases.script:
ln -s missing alias
find -P alias -type l
find -H alias -type l
find -L alias -type l

cases.purpose: Two noncyclic directory spellings are both visited; hardlink aliases are separate results.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/real
printf keep > tree/real/file
ln tree/real/file tree/real/hard
ln -s real tree/alias
find -L tree -type f

cases.purpose: A detected cycle reports failure while an independent later root is still visited.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
ln -s .. tree/sub/back
printf last > last
find -L tree last -type f

cases.purpose: An invalid path component is a diagnosed search failure; later operands still print.
cases.script:
printf data > file
find file/child file

cases.purpose: A depth-zero search reports the starting directory without trying to read its children.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
printf hidden > tree/file
chmod 000 tree
if find tree -maxdepth 0; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
chmod 700 tree
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Stops before descent and a later missing operand.
cases.script:
mkdir tree; : > tree/file
find tree missing -print -quit

cases.purpose: Stops the depth-first traversal without evaluating its parent or later actions.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub; : > tree/sub/file
find tree -depth -print -quit -print

cases.purpose: Negation and disjunction cannot resume evaluation after quit.
cases.script:
mkdir tree; : > tree/file
find tree ! -quit -o -print

cases.purpose: A skipped quit leaves implicit printing active.
cases.script:
: > a; : > b
find a b -name a -o -quit

cases.purpose: Flushes the pending command arguments on quit.
cases.script:
: > a; : > b
find a b -exec printf '%s\n' '{}' + -quit

cases.purpose: Returns failure if the pending command fails during quit.
cases.script:
: > a
find a -exec false '{}' + -quit

cases.purpose: -newermt DATE, -newerXY REF, -anewer and -newer compare the chosen timestamps like GNU (guest pass 1, G13).
cases.script:
touch -d @100 a; touch -d @200 b; touch -d @2000000000 c
find . -newermt 2000-01-01 ! -name . | sort
find . -newermt '1970-01-01 00:02:00Z' ! -name . | sort
find . -newermt @150 ! -name . | sort
find . -newermm a ! -name . | sort
find . -newer b ! -name . | sort
find . -neweram b ! -name . | sort
find . -anewer a ! -name . | sort
find . -newermt '2033-05-18 03:33:20' ! -name . | sort

cases.purpose: -samefile, -inum and -links select by inode and link count (guest pass 1, G13).
cases.script:
touch h1 x; ln h1 h2; mkdir d
find . -samefile h1 | sort
find . -samefile h1 ! -name h1
find . -inum $(stat -c %i h1) | sort
find . -type f -links 2 | sort
find . -type f -links -2
find . -type f -links +1 | sort

cases.purpose: An invalid -newerXY letter, an unparsable date and a missing -samefile reference fail with status 1.
cases.script:
find . -newerqt 2000-01-01 || echo rc=$?
find . -newermt 'not a date at all' || echo rc=$?
find . -samefile missing || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: GNU -printf directives %m %#m %M %T@ %A+ %AT %t %Tk %u %U %g %G %b %k %n %d %y %Y %l %P %H %S, flags/width/precision, octal and \\c escapes (guest pass 2, G32).
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC0 LC_ALL=C
mkdir s; printf abc > s/f; chmod 644 s/f; touch -d @1709622489.25 s/f; ln -s f s/l; ln -s nope s/dang; ln -s loop s/loop; mkfifo s/p; chmod 755 s
find s/f -printf '[%05s|%-5s|%5m|%#m|%05m|%.2f|%-6f|%10T@]
'
find s/f -printf '%t
%T@
%T+
%TT
%TS
%Tk
%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM %Ta %Tb %Tp %TZ %Tz %Ts %Tj %TD %Tc
'
find s -printf '%y %Y %p %l %d %P %H|
' | sort
find s/f -printf '%b %k %n %S %M %m
'
find s/f -printf '%u:%g %U:%G
' | { IFS=' ' read -r names ids; [[ $names == "$(id -un):$(id -gn)" && $ids == "$(id -u):$(id -g)" ]] && echo owner-ok; }
find s -maxdepth 0 -printf '%M %m %#m %y
'; find s/l -printf '%M
'; find s/p -printf '%M %y
'
find s/f -printf 'a	b\101\cZZZ
'; echo

cases.purpose: A lone trailing % is an error (status 1); an unknown directive or escape is warned about and printed literally with status 0 (guest pass 2, G32).
cases.script:
: > f
find f -printf '%' || echo rc=$?
find f -printf '%Q|\q|\n'; echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -daystart, -ipath/-iwholename/-wholename, -regextype with whole-path -regex, -executable/-readable/-writable, -true/-false, -fprint/-fprint0/-fprintf (guest pass 2, G32).
cases.script:
mkdir s; : > s/f; : > s/ab; chmod 755 s/ab; chmod 644 s/f
find s -daystart -mtime 0 | sort
find s/f -daystart -mtime +0 || echo none
find s -ipath S/F; find s -iwholename 'S/A*'; find s -wholename s/f
find s -regex f; find s -regex 's/f'
find s -regextype posix-basic -regex 's/\(a\|f\)b*' | sort
find s -regextype posix-extended -regex 's/(a|f)b*' | sort
find s -regextype bogus -regex x || echo rc=$?
find s -type f -executable; find s -type f -readable | sort; find s -type f -writable | sort
find s/f -true; find s/f -false; find s/f -not -false
find s -name f -fprint out; cat out
find s -fprint0 out0 -false; tr '\0' '|' < out0 | tr -s '|' '\n' | sort
find s -name ab -fprintf outf '%f %m\n'; cat outf

cases.purpose: -newermt reads date -d's strings, including month names (guest pass 2, G32 via the shared date parser).
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC0
touch -d @1709622489 f
find f -newermt 'Mar 5 2024 07:00'
find f -newermt 'Mar 5 2024 08:00'
find f -newermt '03/04/2024'
echo end

cases.purpose: GNU tools answer --help with help on stdout and status 0; find --help used to write usage to stderr or exit nonzero (guest pass 2, G38).
cases.script: find --help >o 2>e; echo rc=$?; [[ -s o && ! -s e ]] && echo stdout-only

cases.purpose: -newermt takes relative date strings: '1 hour ago', 'yesterday', '-30 min' and a negated '-2 hours' (guest pass 3, G43; fixed by the shared date parser of pass 2).
cases.script:
touch -d '3 hours ago' old; touch -d '20 min ago' mid; touch new
for t in '1 hour ago' yesterday '-30 min' '-2 hours'; do
  printf '%s:' "$t"
  for f in old mid new; do [[ -n $(find "$f" -newermt "$t") ]] && printf ' %s' "$f"; done
  echo
done
find old ! -newermt '-2 hours'

cases.purpose: G57: -newermt reads TZ="ZONE" prefixes and zone-plus-offset items as date -d does.
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC0
mkdir t
touch -d '2024-01-01 04:00' t/four
touch -d '2024-01-01 06:00' t/six
find t -type f -newermt 'TZ="UTC+5" 2024-01-01 00:00' | sort
find t -type f -newermt '2024-01-01 08:00 UTC+3' | sort
find t -type f ! -newermt '2024-01-01 00:00 UTC-0500' | sort
